strategyPosture: Stay selective and staged: SPY is -0.6% from its high with loose credit (SLOOS 0%, HY OAS 3.03%), so there is no confirmed rollover to de-risk against — but a 2.92% real 10-year and an IWM tape at -6.45% over 1 month argue against adding broad beta. Work the screened DATA_AHEAD dislocations (AVGO, VRT, BWXT, APP, NOW) with thesis verification before sizing, per the system's RESEARCH_SCREENED pullback posture.

themes.counterRead: The calm is narrow, not broad: IWM is -6.45% over 1 month and -6.93% over 3 months while QQQ is +4.87% over 1 month, so leadership is rotating inside large-cap tech rather than broadening. With credit still loose, this is rotation, not a confirmed rollover — but the divergence itself is the risk to track, because a credit flip would change the read.

themes.label: Index Leadership Rotation, Not Rollover

themes.counterRead: Equity and credit calm is running ahead of what a 2.92% real 10-year would normally permit, so the exposure is to a rates repricing, not a credit event that has already started. HY OAS at 3.03% gives no confirmation of stress; until spreads widen, the rates level alone is a caution flag, not an exit signal.
themes.dataAnchor: Rates say otherwise: DGS10 is 5.28%, DGS2 is 4.79% (2s10s curve +0.49), DGS30 is 5.66%, and the real 10-year yield is 2.92% against 2.36% breakeven inflation (T10YIE). Yet high-yield spreads (HY OAS) sit at 3.03% and DFF is 3.88% — credit is not pricing stress despite the high real-rate level.
themes.label: High Real Rates, Unstressed Credit
themes.narrative: With VIX at 15.7 (down -4.62% over 1 month) and equities near highs, the market is pricing a benign rates backdrop into the Oct 14 CPI print and the Oct 27-28 FOMC decision, both flagged HIGH signal strength in active events.
themes.watchFor: Watch HY OAS widening materially above 3.03% or DGS10 moving above 5.28% into the Oct 14 CPI and Oct 28 FOMC — that combination would convert the rates caution into confirmed stress.

whereWaveBuilds: The next move most likely builds in the dislocated quality/AI-infrastructure complex — AVGO at -23.9% from its high on +55% revenue growth and VRT at -35.1% on +27.7% growth — where fundamentals are already ahead of price.
